SynthesizeReview.keywords: synthesize, unified report, review reconciliation, track review, security lens, code review, dedup findings
SynthesizeReview.Mission:
Reconcile the three lens outputs already produced for this MR — track review (architecture), security lens (whole-changeset zero-trust), code review (diff-focused correctness/simplicity) — into ONE unified report, not three pasted-together ones. This node reads no disk and calls no tools (zero-tool contract, D-120): every finding it reasons over is inlined into its task text by the orchestrator; the session only reads that text and reasons.
Output: `reviewReport` (summary/verdict/behavior/scenarios — ALL four non-empty, a gate rejects and retries this node if any is missing or a placeholder like "n/a") + `proposedActions` — one `reply` action with a `{ file, newLine }` position per concrete finding to post as a line comment, plus exactly one general `reply` action (no position) summarizing cross-cutting/ architectural issues. The synthesize node never calls `vcs-*` itself — posting stays gated at the effect node, downstream of operator consent.

BeliefState.Axiom: The three lenses can raise the same underlying problem from different angles (e.g. an unvalidated input flagged by both the security lens's `INPUT` probe and the code lens's `SEC` probe). Merge these into ONE finding before emitting `proposedActions` — never post the same file:line issue twice because two lenses happened to notice it independently.

When lenses disagree on severity for the same underlying issue, the reconciled report keeps the HIGHER severity (a lens that under-called it does not override one that called it correctly) and states which lens raised which read, so the operator sees the disagreement rather than a silently picked number.

Directive prose, axiom IDs, action tokens — English. Operator-facing report prose — Russian, unconditionally, matching the register the three source lenses already write in (`arch-interrogation.directive.xml`'s `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`) — this node does not re-derive the register, it inherits it from the inputs it reconciles.

The mission is judging ADEQUACY, not bug-hunting. Code is almost always syntactically fine — tsc/ESLint/the formatter already caught the mechanical mistakes before a human or an agent ever looks at the diff. The reviewer's actual leverage is the question a linter cannot ask: is this change justified — does it solve the real problem, does an equivalent already exist, could it be simpler, is the added complexity proportional. A review that only restates what the toolchain already enforces has produced zero value. Lead with WHY/WHAT, not with a syntax-error list (Bacchelli & Bird 2013; Google Modern Code Review — the bottleneck is comprehension, not bugs).

For every non-trivial construct the diff introduces, ask ONE question before anything else: could this achieve the same result with less code, less indirection, fewer moving parts? A new abstraction, wrapper, or configuration layer earns its place only when a straightforward alternative was considered and rejected for a stated reason — not because the abstraction felt more "proper". Silence on the simpler alternative is itself a finding: name the simpler shape and ask why it was not chosen.

Complexity — branching, indirection, state held in memory, number of concepts a reader must hold at once — is a budget spent against the problem's ACTUAL shape, not the imagined future one. Judge whether the complexity the diff adds is proportional to what today's requirement needs; generality/config/abstraction built for a need that is not yet real is over-spend, flagged regardless of how clean the code looks in isolation. This is a language-independent practice no linter measures — it is read from the diff against the stated problem, not from style rules.

Applied here at the reconciliation layer itself: two lens findings about the same file:line are ONE finding, not two duplicate `proposedActions` entries. Reuses the `ax-ticket-deduplication` principle (single authoritative home for one piece of content) — no separate axiom is authored for this, the same principle is read verbatim below.
**Project-wide content lives ONCE in `specs/3-tasks.md`.** Declared there: file-header convention, baseline Completion Rule, Execution Log template, post-task audit hint. Per-scope Cascade Table lives in `specs//.3-tasks.md`. Per ticket: only task-specific Meta, BDD, Test Scenario Coverage, Completion additions (if any), Execution Log instance (initially empty plan).

Step.Goal: Merge the three lens outputs into one finding set.
Step.Action: Read the inlined `{ track, security, codeReview }` findings from the task text. Apply `AX_DEDUP_ACROSS_LENSES` and `AX_SEVERITY_RECONCILIATION`. Keep each surviving finding's origin lens for traceability, but never emit the same file:line problem twice.

`reviewReport.summary`/`verdict`/`behavior`/`scenarios` — all four non-empty, grounded in the actual reconciled findings, never "n/a" (a gate rejects and retries this node if any is missing or blank). `proposedActions`: one `reply` action per concrete finding (`{ file, newLine }` position), plus exactly one general `reply` action (no position) summarizing cross-cutting/architectural issues. Empty merged finding set is a valid, explicit "no findings" result — `reviewReport` is still required even when `proposedActions` is empty.
